title: How the rook moves
summary: Straight lines along ranks and files, any distance, no jumping.

steps.md: The **rook** moves in a straight line along a rank or file, as many empty squares as it likes. It cannot jump: a piece in the way stops it. It is worth about 5 pawns.
From d4 the rook reaches every square on the d-file and the 4th rank: 14 squares.

steps.explain: Along the 4th rank to the right edge in one move: distance does not matter.
Rooks move backwards just as easily as forwards.

steps.question: Can the rook move from d4 to d7 here?
choices: No, the pawn on d6 blocks the way
steps.explain: Rooks cannot jump. The white pawn on d6 blocks the file, so d5 is as far as the rook can go upwards.

steps.prompt: Get the rook from b2 to h8 in two moves. The pawn on b5 blocks the b-file, so find the other route.
steps.hint: First go sideways along the 2nd rank.
steps.explain: Rh2 then Rh8: along the 2nd rank, then up the open h-file. When the direct line is blocked, look for the route via another line.

steps.question: A rook stands alone in the corner (a1) of an empty board. How many squares can it reach?
steps.explain: Always 14 on an empty board (7 along the rank + 7 along the file), whether in the corner or the centre. Unlike other pieces, a rook loses no range on the edge.

steps.question: Retrieval check: can a rook move diagonally?
steps.explain: Rooks move only along ranks and files. Diagonals belong to the bishop.

steps.question: Retrieval check: can a rook jump over a piece in its way?
steps.explain: Only the knight jumps. Rooks, bishops and queens are stopped by any piece in their path.
